references.text: Describes the tablets given to Moses on Mount Sinai, written with God's finger, the same tablets mentioned in Exodus 32:16.
God commands Moses to carve new stone tablets after the first ones were broken, continuing the story of the tablets.
Moses writes the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments, on the tablets—a parallel to God's writing on the original tablets.
Moses recounts that God proclaimed His covenant, the Ten Commandments, and wrote them on two stone tablets.
Describes the tablets written with God's finger, containing the words God spoke from the fire on the mountain.
Tells of the new tablets Moses carved, and how God wrote the Ten Commandments on them again.
Paul contrasts stone tablets with tablets of the heart, referring to the letter of the law written on stone.
Mentions the ark of the covenant which contained the tablets of the law, the same tablets God wrote on.
Continues the same story by describing the storage of the same tablets mentioned in Exodus 32:16.
A theological parallel where Exodus 32:16 serves as the historical basis for the claim in 2 Timothy 3:16 that Scripture is God's own work.
Direct narrative link to the same tablets; shows that God's writing (engraved) endures even when humans break them.
